chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'No mother should be harmed because of her child, and no father because of his child.'

He said: 'The wet nurses used to do this: one of them would push away the man when he wanted to have intercourse, saying, "I will not let you go, for I fear that I will conceive and kill this child of mine that I am nursing." And when the woman called the man, he would say, "I fear that I will have intercourse with you and kill my child," so he would leave her and not have intercourse with her.'
So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, forbade that from happening, that the man should be harmed by the woman and the woman by the man.'
ai.seo_question: What is the historical context of the Quranic verse about no mother being harmed by her child regarding breastfeeding?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq) to clarify the specific historical context of Surah Al-Baqarah 2:233, where wet nurses or their husbands would withhold marital relations to prolong breastfeeding, fearing that conception would lead to weaning and the 'death' of the nursing child. This tafsir highlights the pre-Islamic practice of using breastfeeding as a tool for sexual leverage, which the Quran corrected to prevent mutual harm (tadarur) and ensure the child's welfare. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the practical legal implications of verses in preventing exploitation within family structures.
